samples.notes:
University Physics Lab Report: The Photoelectric Effect and Determination of Planck's Constant

1. Objective
1. To observe the basic laws of the photoelectric effect and verify Einstein's photoelectric equation.
2. To measure the stopping voltage under light of different frequencies and calculate Planck's constant h.

2. Principle
The photoelectric effect is the physical phenomenon in which electrons inside a metal absorb photon energy and escape from the metal surface when light shines on it. Einstein proposed the light-quantum hypothesis, giving each photon an energy E = hν. When incident light strikes the cathode of a phototube with work function W0, the maximum initial kinetic energy of the photoelectrons follows:
Ek = hν − W0 = eUc

3. Data and Analysis
We measured the stopping voltage at five monochromatic wavelengths (365 nm, 405 nm, 436 nm, 546 nm, and 577 nm). A linear fit gave the slope k = h/e, yielding Planck's constant as 6.58 × 10^-34 J·s, a relative error of about 0.75%. The data agree well with the theoretical prediction.

Submitted by: Li Hua
September 11, 2026
samples.reflection:
Dear Teacher,

Hello. Today, with deep guilt and regret, I am writing this sincere letter of self-criticism.

I have reflected carefully on my recent laxness with classroom discipline and homework. As a student, attending class on time, listening attentively, thinking independently, and completing every assignment carefully are my basic duties. Yet because of weak self-control and an irregular schedule lately, my study habits have slipped, and this may even have affected the atmosphere of the whole class.

Here I offer a sincere apology to you and to all my classmates. I have truly recognized my mistake. From now on I will correct my attitude, follow the rules strictly, and make a sensible study plan, bringing my fullest energy to every single class.

Please, teacher and classmates, watch how I do from here on.

Apologetically,
Zhang Yu
September 11, 2026
samples.composition:
The Breeze of That Midsummer

On a summer afternoon, sunlight filtered through the mottled leaves of the plane trees, scattering flecks of broken gold across the bluestone path. Cicadas called tirelessly from the branches, and the air was filled with the fresh scent of grass and gardenias.

That summer in memory always felt long and quiet. Grandma rocked her palm fan in the bamboo chair of the courtyard, softly telling old legends. A wind chime tinkled beneath the eaves, each note like an echo struck deep in time. Time has flown; now, walking the noisy city streets, an occasional warm breeze always carries me back to that quiet courtyard and that gentle, lingering sunset.
samples.english_notebook:
The Old Man and the Sea

He was an old man who fished alone in a skiff in the Gulf Stream and he had gone eighty-four days now without taking a fish. In the first forty days a boy had been with him. But after forty days without a fish the boy's parents had told him that the old man was now definitely and finally salao, which is the worst form of unlucky.

Everything about him was old except his eyes and they were the same color as the sea and were cheerful and undefeated. "Santiago," the boy said to him as they climbed the bank from where the skiff was hauled up. "I could go with you again. We've made some money."
samples.photo_realism:
Notes and Reflections on Reading

Living in a fast-paced age of information overload, we are surrounded every day by fragmented content. Returning to the classics lets us rediscover an inner calm amid a restless world.

As Romain Rolland wrote, "There is only one true heroism in the world: to see the world as it is, and to love it." Reading is not an escape from reality but a way to understand life more deeply and richly. Between the lines, we not only converse with the great minds of the past but also catch sight of our true selves.

Reading notes by: Li Ming
September 11, 2026
samples.vintage_letter:
To see my handwriting is to see me:

I hope this letter finds you well.
I wonder whether the wind outside your window also blows through your city these days. All is well here, though on golden-sunset evenings I sometimes think of the old days when we walked the forest path together.

Time slips by and many stories have scattered with the wind, yet the friendship I treasure remains as warm as ever. May all go smoothly with you, and may ordinary days hold frequent joy. I look forward to the day we meet again and talk over a cup.

Your dear friend, far away
September 11, 2026
